text:
alice.nguyen: FYI — in us-west2 we're seeing sustained NVMe IOPS saturation on the ephemeral pool for ~2h. gpu-attach backlog spiked from 5 -> 120.

ben.kim: grabbing metrics now. which pool? scratchpool-hot or scratchpool-cold?

alice.nguyen: scratchpool-hot. mountpoints: /var/scratch/* on gnode-usw2-xx. logs show repeated block-device timeouts and attach retries.

ben.kim: prometheus query (5m):
```
sum(rate(nvme_io_ops_total{region="us-west2",pool="scratchpool-hot"}[5m]))
```
shows a sustained 85k ops/s vs normal 12k. latency p95 for smallwrites at 60ms.

charu_m: oof. any sign of firmware resets or SMART errors?

alice.nguyen: SMART transient warnings on a subset of nodes but not full drives. 2 nodes flipped read-only yesterday (auto-evict kicked in).

infra-bot: ALERT: gpu-attach-backlog > 100 in us-west2 for 30m (link: https://dash.redwood.example/alerts/1728801234) :warning:

david: Is this correlated with the nightly janitor scrub window? We kicked a region-wide deep-scrub last night to clear tempfiles.

alice.nguyen: Yes — scrub throughput peaked at same time. Janitor concurrency was at 8 for that region.

ben.kim: quick mitigation options:
- lower janitor concurrency to 2 for us-west2
- enable aggressive KV/prefix caching for inference-customer jobs hitting ephemeral
- temporarily divert non-prod GPU batch jobs to dedicated nodes in us-east1
- increase attach timeout fallback to fall through to remote-provision (costly)

charu_m: We already throttle fstrim/trim jobs, but scrub does heavy small writes. Suggest: immediate concurrency drop + rate-limit scrub to 50% of baseline.

alice.nguyen: I'm going to patch janitor config now. Will reduce concurrency to 2 and add a 1s sleep between file ops.

ben.kim: creating canary change:
```
PATCH /infra/janitor/configs/us-west2
{ "concurrency": 2, "per_op_sleep_ms": 1000, "max_ops_per_min": 300 }
```
rolling to 10 nodes first.

oncall-sre: heads up — if we drop concurrency that will push scrub backlog into next window, could increase disk wear long-term. We should monitor backlog growth and schedule an extended low-impact scrub overnight.

alice.nguyen: agreed. short-term safety first. scheduling extended low-IO scrub for 4am-8am with concurrency 1 and off-peak throttle.

david: cost note: diverting batch jobs to other regions will add network egress (~$0.02/token equivalent for heavy runs). If we land on fallback to remote-provision it's ~2-3x inference unit cost. Recommend ops choose targeted job reroutes instead of wholesale failover.

charu_m: also raising a quick telemetry gap: storage-agent on the affected gnodes lost a heartbeat during the spike; we've queued an agent restart on the three worst hosts.

ben.kim: can we preemptively retire the 5 drives with SMART warnings? Replacement will cost time but avoid further read-only flips.

alice.nguyen: opened hardware ticket. will cordon those nodes after current attaches drain (~30m).

infra-bot: NOTE: deploy rolling-patch-janitor-config started (runbook: infra/playbooks/janitor-throttle.md)

oncall-sre: Monitoring checklist (watch):
- nvme_iops_total (pool=scratchpool-hot)
- nvme_io_latency_seconds_bucket p95/p99
- gpu_attach_backlog/us-west2
- janitor_backlog_ops
- SMART error rate per node
- network retransmits (to ensure it's not network-induced IO retries)

alice.nguyen: initial rollout to 10 nodes looks good — iops dropped ~55% and p95 smallwrite latency down to 18ms. gpu-attach backlog decreased to 22.

charu_m: good. leave throttle in place for 2 more hours then slowly ramp concurrency to 4 and observe.

david: after we stabilize: propose creating a region-specific scrub cadence map and a cost/IOPS budget per pool. If a scrub would push pool above budget, fail it or run low-impact mode automatically.

alice.nguyen: +1. I'll draft an RFC for scrub budget + auto-throttle policies and attach the incident timeline. Owner: alice.nguyen. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

ben.kim: followups: hardware ticket #HW-9932, rolling patch id rp-172880A, and we diverted two non-prod jobs to us-east1.

oncall-sre: closing loop — if any node flips RO again, ping me and we'll evac immediately. Thanks everyone :heart:
